why: Fact types extracted since PR 3 (the old prompt on stage names): is the mix still only Capex-Desk types?
sql: select f.fact_type, f.verification_status, count(*) as facts, count(distinct f.company_id) as companies, count(*) filter (where f.as_of >= current_date - 180 and f.superseded_by is null) as current_in_180d, count(*) filter (where f.counterparty is not null) as with_counterparty, min(f.as_of), max(f.as_of) from facts f where f.created_at >= '2026-10-22 17:00+00' group by 1, 2 order by 3 desc;

why: Documents read since PR 3, by rank and kind, and their fact yield. Shows how many documents produce no fact, and how many produce S9-type facts, under the old prompt.
sql: with th as (select distinct company_id from theses where state in ('research', 'thesis', 'position', 'review')), docs as (select d.id, d.company_id, d.kind, d.status, d.published_at, d.text_chars, (select count(*) from facts f where f.document_id = d.id and f.verification_status = 'verified') as v, (select count(*) from facts f where f.document_id = d.id and f.verification_status = 'needs_review') as r, (select count(*) from facts f where f.document_id = d.id and f.fact_type in ('order_win', 'customer_win', 'capacity_addition', 'price_increase', 'lead_time', 'new_segment', 'governance_flag')) as s9_type_any_status from documents d where d.created_at >= '2026-10-22 17:00+00') select case when company_id in (select company_id from th) then 'thesis' else 'stage_or_other' end as reader_rank, kind, status, count(*) as documents, count(distinct company_id) as companies, sum(v) as verified, sum(r) as review, sum(s9_type_any_status) as s9_type_facts, count(*) filter (where v = 0 and r = 0) as documents_without_facts, round(avg(text_chars)) as avg_chars, min(published_at)::date as oldest_published, max(published_at)::date as newest_published from docs group by 1, 2, 3 order by 1, 2, 3;

why: Has any S9-type fact ever been extracted, in any status, including from about 700 Capex-Desk-era documents of AI-infrastructure names that announce orders all the time? Close to zero would back the causal claim about P-01's framing.
sql: select c.market, f.fact_type, f.verification_status, count(*) as facts, count(distinct f.company_id) as companies, count(*) filter (where f.counterparty is not null) as with_counterparty, max(f.as_of) as latest_as_of, max(f.created_at)::date as last_stored from facts f join companies c on c.id = f.company_id where f.fact_type in ('order_win', 'customer_win', 'capacity_addition', 'price_increase', 'lead_time', 'new_segment', 'governance_flag') group by 1, 2, 3 order by 1, 2, 3;

why: Per-company India fundamentals depth (quarters held, newest quarter). Sizes the backfill and tests the oldest-first finding (only 298 of 2,128 have a row filed in the last 200 days).
sql: with f as (select c.id, count(distinct q.period_end) as quarters, min(q.period_end) as first_q, max(q.period_end) as last_q from companies c left join fundamentals_q q on q.company_id = c.id where c.market = 'in' and c.in_universe group by c.id) select quarters, count(*) as companies, count(*) filter (where last_q >= date '2026-06-30') as newest_jun26_or_later, count(*) filter (where last_q < date '2026-03-31') as newest_before_mar26, min(first_q) as earliest_first_q, max(last_q) as latest_last_q from f group by quarters order by quarters;

why: India price and NIFTY history depth. C3 needs a close 52 weeks back (within 14 days) and C1 needs 52+ weekly points; expected: 4 Fridays starting 2026-09-25.
sql: select 'prices_w' as series, count(distinct p.week_end) as weeks, min(p.week_end) as first_week, max(p.week_end) as last_week, count(*) as rows, count(distinct p.company_id) as companies, string_agg(distinct p.source, ',') as sources from prices_w p join companies c on c.id = p.company_id where c.market = 'in' union all select 'benchmarks_w ' || b.symbol, count(distinct b.week_end), min(b.week_end), max(b.week_end), count(*), null, null from benchmarks_w b where b.symbol in ('NIFTY 50', 'NIFTY 500') group by b.symbol;

why: Database headroom before adding about 30-35 MB of India prices, 35-45k fundamentals rows and a state copy (size_guard fails above 400 MB).
sql: select pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database())) as database, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('prices_w')) as prices_w, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('fundamentals_q')) as fundamentals_q, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('ownership_q')) as ownership_q, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('signal_values')) as signal_values, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('corp_events')) as corp_events, (select count(*) from prices_w) as prices_w_rows;

why: Backfill priority: how many India universe names clear the Rs 500 crore candidate floor, where share counts are known.
sql: with px as (select distinct on (p.company_id) p.company_id, p.close from prices_w p join companies c on c.id = p.company_id where c.market = 'in' and c.in_universe order by p.company_id, p.week_end desc), sh as (select distinct on (q.company_id) q.company_id, q.shares_outstanding from fundamentals_q q join companies c on c.id = q.company_id where c.market = 'in' and q.shares_outstanding is not null order by q.company_id, q.period_end desc, q.filed_at desc) select count(*) as priced_universe, count(sh.company_id) as with_shares, count(*) filter (where px.close * sh.shares_outstanding >= 5000000000) as mcap_ge_500cr, count(*) filter (where px.close * sh.shares_outstanding < 5000000000) as mcap_below_500cr from px left join sh on sh.company_id = px.company_id;

why: Stale-quarter scoring: India signal and red-flag hits on 2026-10-16 whose newest stored quarter ended before 2026-03-31 (the freshness guard would mute these).
sql: with latest as (select q.company_id, max(q.period_end) as last_q from fundamentals_q q join companies c on c.id = q.company_id where c.market = 'in' group by q.company_id) select x.rule_id, count(*) as fired, count(*) filter (where l.last_q < date '2026-03-31') as newest_quarter_before_mar26 from (select rv.company_id, rv.flag_id as rule_id from redflag_values rv where rv.week_end = date '2026-10-16' and rv.inputs->>'status' = 'fired' union all select sv.company_id, sv.signal_id from signal_values sv where sv.week_end = date '2026-10-16' and sv.fired) x join companies c on c.id = x.company_id and c.market = 'in' left join latest l on l.company_id = x.company_id group by x.rule_id order by x.rule_id;

why: Size each Watch gate per market at each market's latest scored week, so the revenue gate can be chosen and the 12/8 caps confirmed to bind. Cumulative counts: one family E>=50, no soft flag, market cap floor, Gap known, Gap>=60, revenue not falling; also the two-signal subset, the stricter alternatives (C2 known; ROIC above the 9%/12% discount rate) and how many sit in the bottom decile of 52-week returns.
sql: with wk as ( select c.market, max(s.week_end) as week_end from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id group by c.market ), base as ( select c.market, s.company_id, s.evidence, s.gap, s.bucket, cardinality(s.families) as nf, (m.metrics->>'market_cap')::numeric as mcap, (m.metrics->>'revenue_yoy')::numeric as rev_yoy, (m.metrics->>'roic')::numeric as roic, (select count(*) from redflag_values f where f.company_id = s.company_id and f.week_end = s.week_end and f.inputs->>'status' = 'fired' and not f.hard) as soft, (select (x.inputs->>'score')::numeric from context_values x where x.company_id = s.company_id and x.week_end = s.week_end and x.metric_id = 'C2') as c2, (select x.pct from context_values x where x.company_id = s.company_id and x.week_end = s.week_end and x.metric_id = 'C3') as c3_pct, (select count(*) from signal_values v where v.company_id = s.company_id and v.week_end = s.week_end and v.fired and v.strength > 0) as n_fired from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id join wk on wk.market = c.market and wk.week_end = s.week_end left join company_metrics m on m.company_id = s.company_id and m.week_end = s.week_end ), g as ( select b.*, (b.nf = 1 and b.evidence >= 50 and b.bucket in ('none', 'watch') and b.soft = 0) as ready, coalesce(b.mcap >= case b.market when 'us' then 300000000 else 5000000000 end, false) as cap_ok from base b ) select market, count(*) filter (where nf = 1 and evidence >= 50 and bucket in ('none', 'watch')) as one_family_e50_not_excluded, count(*) filter (where ready) as plus_no_soft_flag, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok) as plus_mcap_floor, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok and gap is not null) as plus_gap_known, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok and gap >= 60) as plus_gap_60, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok and gap >= 60 and coalesce(rev_yoy, 0) >= 0) as plus_revenue_not_falling, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok and gap >= 60 and coalesce(rev_yoy, 0) >= 0 and n_fired >= 2) as of_which_two_signals, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok and gap >= 60 and c2 is not null) as alt_c2_known, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok and gap >= 60 and roic >= case market when 'us' then 0.09 else 0.12 end) as alt_roic_above_discount, count(*) filter (where ready and cap_ok and gap >= 60 and c3_pct < 10) as bottom_decile_52w_return from g group by market order by market;

why: The would-be Watch list per market (top 30) under the proposed rank, ranked both without and with the revenue gate. Shows depth, signals, C1-C3 scores, the 52-week return percentile, revenue growth, ROIC, share change and market cap, so a PM can read the value-trap exposure (for example, whether CHTR or ENPH drop out on the revenue gate).
sql: with wk as ( select c.market, max(s.week_end) as week_end from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id group by c.market ), base as ( select c.market, coalesce(c.ticker, c.nse_symbol, c.name) as code, c.sector, s.company_id, s.evidence, s.gap, (m.metrics->>'market_cap')::numeric as mcap, (m.metrics->>'revenue_yoy')::numeric as rev_yoy, (m.metrics->>'roic')::numeric as roic, (m.metrics->>'share_change_yoy')::numeric as shares_yoy, (select coalesce(sum(t.strength), 0) from ( select v.strength from signal_values v where v.company_id = s.company_id and v.week_end = s.week_end and v.fired order by v.strength desc limit 2) t) as depth, (select string_agg(v.signal_id || ':' || round(v.strength, 2), ' ' order by v.signal_id) from signal_values v where v.company_id = s.company_id and v.week_end = s.week_end and v.fired) as signals, (select jsonb_object_agg(x.metric_id, round((x.inputs->>'score')::numeric, 0)) from context_values x where x.company_id = s.company_id and x.week_end = s.week_end) as context_scores, (select round(x.pct, 0) from context_values x where x.company_id = s.company_id and x.week_end = s.week_end and x.metric_id = 'C3') as c3_return_pct, (select count(*) from redflag_values f where f.company_id = s.company_id and f.week_end = s.week_end and f.inputs->>'status' = 'fired') as flags, exists (select 1 from scores p where p.company_id = s.company_id and p.week_end = s.week_end - 7 and cardinality(p.families) = 1 and p.evidence >= 50 and p.gap >= 60) as eligible_last_week from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id join wk on wk.market = c.market and wk.week_end = s.week_end left join company_metrics m on m.company_id = s.company_id and m.week_end = s.week_end where cardinality(s.families) = 1 and s.evidence >= 50 and s.bucket in ('none', 'watch') and s.gap >= 60 ), ranked as ( select b.*, row_number() over (partition by b.market order by b.evidence desc, b.depth desc, b.gap desc, b.company_id) as rank_all, coalesce(b.rev_yoy, 0) >= 0 as revenue_ok from base b where b.flags = 0 and coalesce(b.mcap >= case b.market when 'us' then 300000000 else 5000000000 end, false) ), ranked2 as ( select r.*, case when r.revenue_ok then row_number() over (partition by r.market, r.revenue_ok order by r.evidence desc, r.depth desc, r.gap desc, r.company_id) end as rank_with_revenue_gate from ranked r ) select market, rank_all, rank_with_revenue_gate, code, sector, evidence, round(depth, 2) as depth, signals, round(gap, 1) as gap, context_scores, c3_return_pct, round(rev_yoy, 3) as revenue_yoy, round(roic, 3) as roic, round(shares_yoy, 3) as share_change_yoy, round(mcap / 1e6) as mcap_millions, eligible_last_week from ranked2 where rank_all <= 30 order by market, rank_all;

why: Week-over-week churn of the pure-rank top 12 over the last 5 US weeks, including names dropped on Gap alone at unchanged depth. This justifies putting last week's names ahead of Gap-only reshuffles. The market cap and revenue gates are omitted because company_metrics keeps only the latest week.
sql: with weeks as ( select distinct s.week_end from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id where c.market = 'us' order by 1 desc limit 5 ), elig as ( select s.week_end, s.company_id, s.evidence, s.gap, (select coalesce(sum(t.strength), 0) from ( select v.strength from signal_values v where v.company_id = s.company_id and v.week_end = s.week_end and v.fired order by v.strength desc limit 2) t) as depth from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id join weeks w on w.week_end = s.week_end where c.market = 'us' and cardinality(s.families) = 1 and s.evidence >= 50 and s.bucket in ('none', 'watch') and s.gap >= 60 and not exists (select 1 from redflag_values f where f.company_id = s.company_id and f.week_end = s.week_end and f.inputs->>'status' = 'fired') ), ranked as ( select e.*, row_number() over (partition by e.week_end order by e.evidence desc, e.depth desc, e.gap desc, e.company_id) as rk from elig e ) select a.week_end, count(*) as eligible, count(*) filter (where a.rk <= 12) as top12, count(*) filter (where a.rk <= 12 and b.rk <= 12) as still_top12_from_last_week, count(*) filter (where b.rk <= 12) as last_weeks_top12_still_eligible, count(*) filter (where b.rk <= 12 and a.rk > 12 and a.depth = b.depth) as dropped_on_gap_alone from ranked a left join ranked b on b.company_id = a.company_id and b.week_end = a.week_end - 7 group by a.week_end order by a.week_end desc;

why: R4 at the latest US week, by share source and size band: how many are in the stage, how many saturated one-family names R4 alone keeps off Watch, and how many two-family names R4 alone holds below 60.
sql: with wk as ( select max(s.week_end) as w from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id where c.market = 'us' ), r4 as ( select f.company_id, f.inputs->>'shares_source' as source, (f.inputs->>'share_change_yoy')::numeric as yoy, jsonb_array_length(coalesce(f.inputs->'splits', '[]'::jsonb)) > 0 as split_seen, s.evidence, cardinality(s.families) as nf, s.bucket, (select count(*) from redflag_values g where g.company_id = f.company_id and g.week_end = f.week_end and g.inputs->>'status' = 'fired' and not g.hard) as soft from redflag_values f join wk on f.week_end = wk.w join scores s on s.company_id = f.company_id and s.week_end = f.week_end join companies c on c.id = f.company_id where c.market = 'us' and f.flag_id = 'R4' and f.inputs->>'status' = 'fired' ) select source, case when yoy < 0.2 then 'a 10-20 pct' when yoy < 0.5 then 'b 20-50 pct' when yoy < 1 then 'c 50-100 pct' else 'd 100+ pct' end as band, count(*) as fired, count(*) filter (where split_seen) as split_seen, count(*) filter (where evidence >= 40) as in_stage, count(*) filter (where nf = 1 and soft = 1 and bucket in ('none', 'watch') and evidence + 10 >= 50) as watch_ready_but_for_r4, count(*) filter (where nf >= 2 and soft = 1 and evidence < 60 and evidence + 10 >= 60) as two_family_held_below_60_only_by_r4 from r4 group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2;

why: Are R4's diluted-share fires real issuance? Compares them with the cover-page shares outstanding a year apart, and counts loss-to-profit swings (the antidilution artifact). Read-only diagnostic: it takes fundamentals_q's latest version filed before the week's cutoff, the way as_of() does.
sql: with wk as ( select max(s.week_end) as w from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id where c.market = 'us' ), r4 as ( select f.company_id, (f.inputs->>'share_change_yoy')::numeric as diluted_yoy from redflag_values f join wk on f.week_end = wk.w join companies c on c.id = f.company_id where c.market = 'us' and f.flag_id = 'R4' and f.inputs->>'status' = 'fired' and f.inputs->>'shares_source' = 'diluted_shares' and jsonb_array_length(coalesce(f.inputs->'splits', '[]'::jsonb)) = 0 ), q as ( select distinct on (fq.company_id, fq.period_end) fq.company_id, fq.period_end, fq.shares_outstanding, fq.net_income from fundamentals_q fq join r4 on r4.company_id = fq.company_id cross join wk where fq.filed_at < ((wk.w + 1)::timestamp at time zone 'UTC') order by fq.company_id, fq.period_end, fq.filed_at desc ), n as ( select q.*, row_number() over (partition by q.company_id order by q.period_end desc) as k from q ), per as ( select r4.company_id, r4.diluted_yoy, max(n.shares_outstanding) filter (where n.k = 1) as so_now, max(n.shares_outstanding) filter (where n.k = 5) as so_year_ago, sum(n.net_income) filter (where n.k between 1 and 4) as ni_ttm, sum(n.net_income) filter (where n.k between 5 and 8) as ni_ttm_year_ago, count(n.net_income) filter (where n.k between 1 and 8) as ni_quarters from r4 left join n on n.company_id = r4.company_id group by r4.company_id, r4.diluted_yoy ) select count(*) as r4_on_diluted_no_split, count(*) filter (where so_now > 0 and so_year_ago > 0) as with_cover_counts, count(*) filter (where so_year_ago > 0 and so_now / so_year_ago - 1 >= 0.10) as cover_also_up_10pct, count(*) filter (where so_year_ago > 0 and so_now / so_year_ago - 1 < 0.05) as cover_up_under_5pct, count(*) filter (where ni_quarters = 8 and ni_ttm_year_ago <= 0 and ni_ttm > 0) as loss_to_profit, count(*) filter (where ni_quarters = 8 and ni_ttm_year_ago <= 0 and ni_ttm > 0 and so_year_ago > 0 and so_now / so_year_ago - 1 < 0.05) as loss_to_profit_and_cover_flat from per;

why: Which single soft flag holds saturated one-family names (family sum >= 1) below 50, per market: the Watch supply each flag removes. Tells whether R4 or R2 noise matters.
sql: with wk as ( select c.market, max(s.week_end) as week_end from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id group by c.market ) select c.market, f.flag_id, count(*) as saturated_one_family_names_blocked_only_by_this_flag from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id join wk on wk.market = c.market and wk.week_end = s.week_end join redflag_values f on f.company_id = s.company_id and f.week_end = s.week_end and f.inputs->>'status' = 'fired' and not f.hard where cardinality(s.families) = 1 and s.bucket in ('none', 'watch') and s.evidence >= 40 and (select count(*) from redflag_values g where g.company_id = s.company_id and g.week_end = s.week_end and g.inputs->>'status' = 'fired' and not g.hard) = 1 and (select coalesce(sum(t.strength), 0) from (select v.strength from signal_values v where v.company_id = s.company_id and v.week_end = s.week_end and v.fired order by v.strength desc limit 2) t) >= 1 group by 1, 2 order by 1, 3 desc;

why: Confirms across all retained weeks that no one-family score exceeds 50, i.e. the 55 cap never binds under w0-equal. This backs the funnel copy fix.
sql: select c.market, max(s.evidence) filter (where cardinality(s.families) = 1) as max_one_family_evidence, count(*) filter (where cardinality(s.families) = 1 and s.evidence > 50) as one_family_above_50, count(distinct s.week_end) as weeks_retained from scores s join companies c on c.id = s.company_id group by c.market order by c.market;

why: Which names S8 fires for on stale data at the latest US week, with the holder counts and growth behind each, and whether S7 also fired (if it did, the name keeps its behavior family whatever happens to S8). Shows which candidate/priced_in/stage names depend on March 2026 holdings.
sql: select c.ticker, sv.strength, sv.inputs -> 'holders' as holders, sv.inputs -> 'qoq' as qoq, sv.inputs -> 'pct_in_size_decile' as pct_in_size_decile, s.evidence, s.gap, s.families, s.bucket, exists (select 1 from signal_values s7 where s7.company_id = sv.company_id and s7.week_end = sv.week_end and s7.signal_id = 'S7' and s7.fired) as s7_also_fired from signal_values sv join companies c on c.id = sv.company_id left join scores s on s.company_id = sv.company_id and s.week_end = sv.week_end where c.market = 'us' and sv.week_end = date '2026-10-23' and sv.signal_id = 'S8' and sv.fired order by s.evidence desc nulls last;
